title: How do rainbows form?
examples: Teacher, why do rainbows always appear in the same order?
Does the size of the raindrop change the rainbow?
Can I see a rainbow if it is cloudy?

explain.say: Light travels in straight lines when it is in the air.
When light enters a raindrop, it bends in a process called refraction.
Inside the raindrop, the light bounces off the back surface; this is reflection.
The light then leaves the drop, bending again as it exits the water.
The raindrops act like tiny prisms, separating white light into its colours.
The colours always appear in a specific order, from red on the outside to violet on the inside.

draw.text: Order: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet

faq.q: Why is the order of colours always the same?
faq.a: The order is determined by how much each colour bends when it leaves the raindrop. Violet light bends the most, and red light bends the least.
asks: What makes the colours line up like that?
Does the bending angle change the colour order?

faq.q: Do I need the sun to be behind me to see a rainbow?
faq.a: Yes, the sun must be behind you for the light to shine through the raindrops to your eyes. This is because the light needs a source to bend.
asks: Which way should I face to see one?

faq.q: Can a rainbow appear if there is no rain?
faq.a: No, you need water droplets in the air, like from rain or mist, for the light to bend and reflect properly. The drops are essential for the show.
asks: Do the drops have to be big?
Is mist enough to make a rainbow?

faq.q: Is the rainbow itself a physical object I can touch?
faq.a: No, a rainbow is an optical illusion created by light interacting with water droplets. You are seeing the light path, not a solid thing.
asks: Can I reach out and grab it?
Is it just light playing tricks?

faq.q: Does the colour of the light change the rainbow?
faq.a: The colour of the light source, like sunlight, determines the colours seen. White sunlight contains all the colours in the visible spectrum.
asks: If the sun was yellow, would the rainbow be different?

facts: White sunlight is actually made up of all the colours of the rainbow.
Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another.
Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface.
The colour red bends the least, and violet bends the most.

quiz.say: When sunlight hits a raindrop, what process first bends the light?
quiz.show: Refraction bends light entering the drop.
quiz.why: Refraction is the scientific term for light bending when it changes speed, like entering water.

wrong.0: Bouncing is too general; refraction is the specific name for the initial bend.
wrong.2: Reflection is the bouncing back of light, which happens second inside the drop.
wrong.3: Spectrum is the name of the band of colours, not the action of bending.

quiz.say: If you see the sun behind you, where will the rainbow appear?
quiz.why: The light must travel from the sun, through the drops, and into your eyes from the opposite direction.

wrong.0: If it is behind the sun, the light cannot travel to your eyes.
wrong.1: The rainbow forms in an arc across the sky, not just directly above.
wrong.2: While it can be low, it is defined by the angle relative to the sun, not just the ground.

quiz.say: What is the order of colours seen in the rainbow?

options.show: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet
options.say: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet

quiz.why: This specific order is because red light bends the least, and violet light bends the most, creating the visible spectrum.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because it does not include the full range of colours seen.
wrong.2: This is backwards; the most bent colour (violet) is on the inside.
wrong.3: This only names a small part of the colours and misses the ends.
